articles.title: George thought his funeral was paid for – but now his wife will get nothing when he dies
articles.summary: George Davies made payments to an insurance company for 17 years, but now he isn't entitled to a penny.
articles.body:
For 17 years, George Davies made payments to an insurance company to cover the cost of his funeral.

The 82-year-old, who has stage 4 cancer, thought he had prepared and provided for his wife Marion.

George took the policy out through his local credit union, but it was cancelled after the company backing the product pulled out of the UK.

Credit unions say the closure of the plan has left thousands of people like George in limbo, with many unable to arrange an affordable alternative because they are elderly or unwell.

A coalition of 17 credit unions across Scotland and the north of England is calling for those affected to receive fair compensation.

George, from Bellshill in North Lanarkshire, is currently undergoing palliative care after being diagnosed with oesophageal cancer in 2023.

He says he can't sleep at night because of worrying about how his wife of 50 years will cope when he's gone.

"I needed something to leave to Marion so that she didn't have to worry about funeral expenses," he says.

"The only consolation is that when I die, I stop worrying about it. I just worry about it all the time."

George had been paying into a policy called the Family Protection Plan (FPP), which he took out through Mosshill Credit Union.

He initially thought it was "excellent", promising a cash lump sum on death to policy holders and up to five named family members.

But as his health deteriorates, George says he feels resentful towards the insurance companies involved.

"How can these people do these things?" he asks. "I'm going to need this money sooner than later."

The FFP was a renewable life insurance product which did not build up a cash value over time and could be cancelled with 30 days' notice.

It closed in November 2025, leaving about 5,000 people across the UK without cover.

The Family Protection Plan was first offered in 1999 and closed to new business in 2009, with cover continuing for those already on the scheme.

Although the money could be used for any purpose, BBC Scotland News understands that it was initially advertised to help cover the cost of funerals.

An early leaflet, provided to us by the credit unions, says the FPP could be used for "any of the costs associated with the funeral" – including the wake and travel expenses for relatives.

It was sold exclusively through credit unions to their members.

Credit unions are not-for-profit financial institutions where members pool their savings to lend to one another. They are often community-based and offer an alternative to traditional banking.

FPP was offered by insurance broker CMutual, which was formerly known as CUNA Mutual Group.

The underwriters on the policy changed over the years, with Maiden Life covering the plan between 2022 and 2025.

Maiden Life announced it would leave the UK market in 2024 and gave notice of termination.

CMutual was unable to find another suitable insurer and the plan closed in November 2025.

The coalition of credit unions group says it represents about 1,500 people who have been affected by the closure. Some have paid premiums for up to 25 years.

Julie Reddin is the chief executive of Mosshill credit union and co-chairs the coalition, which is campaigning for members to receive a fair pay out.

She says it is a "scandal" that so many people have lost out on what they regarded as funeral cover.

"We would just like the people that have made money out of the policies to actually stand up and be accountable and not step back and say no that wasn't us," she says.

"It may not have been illegal what they did, but it was immoral."

Credit unions in the coalition have agreed to help with the cost of funerals for affected members as a goodwill gesture as they feel a level of responsibility.

At the time the FPP closed, Julie's branch had 139 members with the policy. She says many are now nearing the end of their life – like George.

"We've had 11 people pass away since the policy closed at a cost of £58,000 to our credit union," she says.

Julie estimates it would cost Mosshill Credit Union £1.3m to cover all policies.

"If we had to pay that out straight away, the credit union would go into liquidation. We just don't have that type of money to pay out," she said.

Julie says the Financial Conduct Authority should have stepped in sooner and wants financial redress for the most vulnerable customers to be split between credit unions, CMutual and Maiden Life.

"Legislation needs to be changed - this should never be able to happen again," she added.

Credit union trade body Altogether Money receives payment from CMutual for offering products through credit unions.

A spokesperson for Altogether Money said the family protection plan had been an optional product that credit unions could choose to offer.

"The decision as to whether or not to offer such products to credit union members has always been one for individual credit union boards to determine and they are responsible for their regulatory compliance and due diligence in relation to these products," it said.

"Some have taken decisions to provide financial ex-gratia payments as a goodwill gesture but in doing so are only concerned to support their members as co-operative, member-owned organisations and do not admit any liability.

"Each credit union should consider its own financial, legal and regulatory position in offering such support and we are providing advice and guidance to credit unions that wish to do so."

The Financial Conduct Authority investigated the cancellation of the plan, and acknowledged the closure had caused "real worry" to those affected.

"We have looked carefully at the circumstances. Based on this evidence, we have decided against taking further action in relation to historical conduct at this time," said a spokesperson.

"This was a renewable life insurance product, meaning that the insurer was not required to provide it indefinitely – and we don't have the power to make them continue.

"We know this is disappointing. We have strongly encouraged the firms involved to help impacted consumers and will support them to achieve this."

The coalition of credit unions will hold a meeting on Wednesday with the UK Treasury, which previously said it was holding talks with the industry and encouraging those involved to "explore all options" to support those affected.

In a statement issued in 2025, Maiden Life said the interests of CMutual's clients and policyholders had been "foremost in our plans" during its dealings with the insurance broker.

"As part of closing our life business we ensured we gave CMutual considerable notice to enable them to inform and provide their customers with alternative arrangements," it said.

A spokesperson for CMutual said the FPP had been "much valued" by credit unions and their members.

It said more than 70% of those holding a policy had claimed at least once, and over 25% had claimed more than once. The FPP enabled the policyholder to claim after the death of other people named on the policy.

CMutual also said the FCA had concluded that many people aged 80 and under were likely to be able to secure other insurance cover.

"Credit unions across the United Kingdom have a tremendous record of supporting and safeguarding their members, and we remain instrumental in helping them achieve this," it said.

"For those members and insureds most affected by the withdrawal of FPP, including those aged over 80 years for whom alternative cover may not be widely available, we remain supportive of both individual credit union initiatives already implemented and sector wide discussions to support such members."

articles.title: Defesa Civil emite alerta severo após alagamentos em Várzea Grande | G1
articles.standfirst: Alguns moradores de Cuiabá também receberam a mensagem por causa da proximidade com Várzea Grande. No distrito do Aguaçu, na capital, foram mobilizadas equipes para resgatar moradores ilhados.
articles.summary: Alguns moradores de Cuiabá também receberam a mensagem por causa da proximidade com Várzea Grande. Na capital, foram mobilizadas equipes para resgatar moradores ilhados.
articles.body:
Chuvas intensas atingiram Várzea Grande nesta quarta-feira (18) — Foto: Defesa Civil de Mato Grosso

A Defesa Civil de Mato Grosso enviou um alerta severo aos moradores de Várzea Grande , na região metropolitana de Cuiabá , após a chuva intensa que atingiu o município na manhã desta quarta-feira (18). A mensagem foi solicitada pela Defesa Civil municipal, que registrou alagamentos e quedas de árvores em alguns bairros .

Por causa da proximidade entre as duas cidades, alguns moradores de Cuiabá também receberam a mensagem. Até o momento, segundo a Defesa Civil estadual, não havia indicação de envio de um alerta severo específico para a capital.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) mantém um alerta de temporais para várias regiões de Mato Grosso até sexta-feira (20) . Há possibilidade de rajadas de vento de até 60 km/h e risco de falta de energia.

A Defesa Civil orienta quem mora perto de córregos a acompanhar o nível da água e se afastar de áreas com sinais de risco. Durante a chuva, a recomendação é evitar atravessar trechos alagados, buscar abrigo longe de árvores e evitar estacionar perto de torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda, que podem cair.

Durante e após o temporal, a orientação é manter distância de postes, cercas e estruturas metálicas e nunca tocar em fios caídos na rua.

Em Cuiabá, a Defesa Civil, o Centro Integrado de Operações Aéreas (Ciopaer) e o Corpo de Bombeiros montaram uma operação para resgatar pessoas que ficaram ilhadas no distrito do Aguaçu. Moradores chegaram a suspeitar do rompimento de uma barragem na região do Manso, mas o Corpo de Bombeiros descartou essa hipótese .

Segundo os bombeiros, a chuva forte fez o nível do rio subir e provocou os alagamentos. De acordo com Ibraim Fantin, pesquisador da Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso (UFMT), o Rio Coxipó-açu subiu 1,62 metro em duas horas .

Entre as ações em andamento estão a instalação de um posto de comando na área atingida e o emprego de equipes de busca, embarcações, viaturas e drones, utilizados no monitoramento da região e na localização de possíveis vítimas. A operação também conta com uma aeronave do Ciopaer, que realiza sobrevoos para avaliar a extensão da área atingida e auxiliar na orientação das equipes em solo.

A Prefeitura de Cuiabá informou que a Secretaria Municipal de Assistência Social já está encaminhando colchões, cobertores e alimentação para atender às famílias afetadas .

articles.title: Muro desaba sobre motos estacionadas e destrói veículos; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu na região portuária de Santos (SP).
articles.summary: Acidente ocorreu na região portuária de Santos (SP).
articles.body:
Um muro de galpão desabou e atingiu motos estacionadas em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo. Vídeos obtidos pelo g1 mostram que os veículos ficaram extremamente danificados após serem soterrados pelos escombros ( assista acima) . Apesar do susto, ninguém ficou ferido.

O acidente ocorreu nesta terça-feira (17), em um galpão localizado entre as avenidas Silvério de Souza e Conde D'Eu, na região portuária. Ao g1 , a vigilante Ana Claudia de Souza Vieira contou que costuma estacionar a moto em frente ao imóvel para ir trabalhar, já que presta serviços em um posto próximo ao local.

A mulher estava voltando do horário de almoço quando soube do ocorrido. "Escutei o barulho e os caminhoneiros falaram: 'caiu o muro', 'caiu o muro', aí eu voltei e vi o desabamento", relembrou a vigilante.

Muro desabou em cima de motocicletas em Santos — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

De acordo com ela, o muro caiu após ser atingido pelo maquinário de uma empresa, que realizava limpeza do imóvel. No entanto, as autoridades não se manifestaram sobre a causa do desabamento.

Segundo Ana, a moto dela e aproximadamente outros 14 veículos foram atingidos pelos destroços do muro. Eles ficaram soterrados por algum tempo, até serem retirados parcialmente destruídos.

A moto dela, por exemplo, foi danificada em diversas partes. A vigilante precisou deixar o veículo no local. Ela contou que aguarda posicionamento da empresa responsável pela limpeza, que ficou de se manifestar para os donos dos veículos, mas também pretende registrar um boletim de ocorrência.

A Prefeitura de Santos informou que a Defesa Civil, a Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) e o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) não foram acionados.

Em nota, a Multilixo informou que, durante um serviço de remoção de resíduos, uma de suas pás-carregadeiras entrou em contato com um muro, que cedeu e atingiu motocicletas estacionadas no local. Apesar disso, não houve feridos nem obstrução da via.

"A empresa concluiu a limpeza do local e está acompanhando a situação para orientar os proprietários das motocicletas sobre as providências relativas aos danos materiais. A companhia também reforça que realiza treinamentos periódicos para os profissionais da operação, com apoio de sua área de Segurança do Trabalho".

Ainda em nota, a Multilixo lamentou o ocorrido e os transtornos causados. A empresa reafirmou compromisso com "a segurança de suas operações e com o atendimento responsável e respeitoso aos envolvidos".

Procurada pelo g1 , a Autoridade Portuária de Santos (APS) não se manifestou até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Ponto Turístico Oficial, Novo Mercadão une gastronomia e compras em Ri | G1
articles.standfirst: Complexo na Zona Sul atrai visitantes de toda a região com culinária plural, opções de presentes, empórios, ambiente confortável e estacionamento gratuito.
articles.summary: Complexo na Zona Sul atrai visitantes de toda a região com culinária plural, opções de presentes, empórios, ambiente confortável e estacionamento gratuito.
articles.body:
Ponto Turístico Oficial, Novo Mercadão une gastronomia e compras em Ribeirão — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Reconhecido oficialmente pela Prefeitura como Ponto Turístico de Ribeirão Preto, o Novo Mercadão da Cidade celebra 18 anos em outubro de 2026 consolidado como uma parada obrigatória tanto para os moradores locais quanto para os visitantes que chegam de diversas cidades da região. Localizado na Zona Sul do município, o empreendimento transformou a tradição dos mercados municipais em um passeio completo de lazer, cultura e compras, reunindo mais de 40 lojistas que traduzem a hospitalidade e a riqueza de sabores do interior paulista.

Diferente dos centros comerciais convencionais, o espaço foi planejado para proporcionar uma experiência acolhedora, onde o visitante caminha sem pressa por corredores charmosos e encontra, em um único endereço, desde alta gastronomia e lembranças criativas até serviços essenciais para o dia a dia.

Gastronomia plural embalada por música ao vivo

A vocação turística do Novo Mercadão ganha força na sua praça de alimentação, que funciona como um verdadeiro polo gastronômico capaz de agradar a todos os paladares da família na mesma mesa. As operações oferecem cardápios variados desde a manhã até a noite, incluindo pratos executivos caprichados, receitas tradicionais portuguesas, culinária oriental, cortes bovinos especiais e porções clássicas e modernas de boteco, sempre acompanhadas do tradicional chope tirado na temperatura ideal.

Para quem busca uma pausa deliciosa durante a tarde ou deseja encerrar a refeição com um toque doce, o complexo conta com cafeterias acolhedoras, gelaterias artesanais e docerias finas. Toda essa jornada de sabores fica ainda mais especial graças à programação gratuita de música ao vivo na praça de alimentação, que embala o público nos encontros noturnos durante a semana e nos horários de almoço aos finais de semana sem cobrança de couvert artístico.

Opções de presentes, lembranças e o charme dos empórios

Como todo bom passeio turístico pede uma recordação especial para levar na bagagem ou surpreender alguém querido, o Novo Mercadão abriga lojas especializadas em casa de presentes, perfumes, relógios, artigos de decoração, lembranças e utilidades domésticas. Essa variedade permite encontrar desde mimos delicados para datas comemorativas até itens funcionais que encantam pela originalidade e pelo bom gosto.

Os amantes da boa mesa também encontram nos empórios do complexo uma excelente oportunidade para montar cestas personalizadas ou presentear com produtos selecionados. As prateleiras reúnem uma curadoria completa de queijos artesanais, castanhas, vinhos nacionais e importados, conservas, azeites, embutidos e especiarias, dividindo os corredores com bancas de hortifrúti, sucos naturais, lojas de produtos saudáveis e suplementos, açougues de cortes nobres e carnes temperadas, além de peixarias abastecidas com o tradicional bacalhau e frutos do mar.

Diferenciais de conforto que fazem a diferença no passeio

Para garantir que a visita seja prazerosa do início ao fim em qualquer época do ano, o Novo Mercadão oferece uma infraestrutura moderna que prioriza o bem-estar do público. O complexo investe continuamente em conforto e já aprovou a instalação de um novo sistema de climatização, que vai proteger ainda mais os frequentadores do calor característico de Ribeirão Preto enquanto passeiam pelas vitrines ou aproveitam a praça de alimentação.

A comodidade é completa com o estacionamento próprio, gratuito, seguro e com áreas cobertas bem próximas às portas de acesso, somado a corredores planos e largos que assegurem acessibilidade integral para famílias com crianças de colo, idosos e portadores de necessidades especiais. Caso o visitante precise resolver alguma pendência prática durante o passeio, o complexo ainda dispõe de estética automotiva, farmácia, casa lotérica, relojoaria, chaveiro e assistência para celular no mesmo local.

Parte desse cuidado vem da gestão profissional da Mafra Gestão Integrada, que administra o empreendimento desde abril de 2026. Marcia Mafra, síndica profissional e diretora da empresa, lidera um plano de melhorias que valoriza a experiência do visitante e fortalece o Novo Mercadão como cartão-postal de Ribeirão Preto.

O espaço também está de portas abertas para novos negócios: há boxes disponíveis para locação, uma oportunidade para empreendedores que desejam fazer parte de um ponto turístico com público fiel e fluxo diário. Interessados podem entrar em contato pelas redes sociais oficiais ( @novomercadaorp ).

articles.title: Chuva em Betim: Defesa Civil atende alagamentos e quedas de muros | G1
articles.standfirst: Até as 10h16, o órgão havia recebido 21 ocorrências. Entre elas estão, ao menos, de cinco desabamentos de muros além de diversos imóveis alagados.
articles.summary: Chuva em Betim provoca transbordamento de riachos, alaga casas e mobiliza a Defesa Civil após 21 chamados de emergência e quedas de muros na cidade.
articles.body:
Betim, na Grande BH, registra ao menos cinco quedas de muros após chuvas fortes — Foto: Globocop/ TV Globo

A Defesa Civil de Betim se mobiliza no início desta tarde de quarta-feira (18) para atender chamados relacionados às fortes chuvas que atingiram a cidade na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte .

Até as 10h16, o órgão havia recebido 21 ocorrências ( veja a lista de locais abaixo ). Entre elas estão, ao menos, de cinco desabamentos de muros além de diversos imóveis alagados.

Nesta amanhã o transbordamento em pontos do Riacho das Areias e da Bacia dos Alterosas, causou a interdição de ruas e avenidas . Uma caminhonete ser arrastada para dentro de um córrego. O motorista, Daniel da Silva Pinto, de 45 anos, conseguiu sair do veículo antes de ser levado pela água e foi encaminhado para um hospital da Unimed.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil, para prestar apoio à população, são realizadas intervenções junto a equipes da Empresa de Construções, Obras, Serviços, Projetos, Transportes e Trânsito de Betim (Ecos), da Transbetim e da Guarda Municipal.

articles.title: Acidente com caminhão em Arealva deixa trânsito em pare e siga | G1
articles.standfirst: Tráfego precisou operar em sistema 'pare e siga' no km 10, na manhã desta quarta-feira (18). Em Jaú (SP), outro tombamento deixou motorista levemente ferido na Rodovia Antônio Prado Galvão de Barros (SP-304).
articles.summary: Acidente com caminhão em Arealva interdita pista no Acesso Agostinho Pereira de Oliveira, enquanto em Jaú outro tombamento deixou um motorista ferido nesta quarta.
articles.body:
Caminhão tomba na manhã de quarta-feira (18) em um trevo na altura do km 10 do Acesso Agostinho Pereira de Oliveira, em Arealva (SP) — Foto: Câmera de segurança/Reprodução

Um caminhão tombou na manhã desta quarta-feira (18), no trevo do km 10 da estrada vicinal Agostinho Pereira de Oliveira, no sentido Pirajuí (SP), em Arealva (SP). A via liga o centro urbano de Arealva à Rodovia Cezário José de Castilho (SP-321).

De acordo com o Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem (DER-SP), a pista no sentido capital-interior foi interditada e o tráfego flui em sistema "pare e siga" pela faixa contrária, sem registro de congestionamento.

Uma viatura brigadista e um guincho da Unidade Básica de Atendimento (UBA) foram enviados ao local para prestar assistência. O estado de saúde do motorista não foi informado.

Motorista de um caminhão teve ferimentos leves depois de um acidente na manhã de quarta-feira (18) em rodovia de Jaú (SP) — Foto: Portal CCM — ARTESP (ccm.artesp.sp.gov.br)

O motorista de outro caminhão teve ferimentos leves depois de um acidente também na manhã desta quarta-feira (18), no km 293 da Rodovia Antônio Prado Galvão de Barros, em Jaú (SP).

De acordo com a concessionária responsável pelo trecho, o veículo tombou e a pista precisou ser interditada. O trânsito foi desviado pelo acostamento até a liberação total da rodovia, por volta das 9h40.

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3087: 18 apostas de Sergipe ganham prêmios na quadra | G1
articles.standfirst: O prêmio para o ganhador da edição desta terça-feira (17) era de R$ 32,1 milhões, mas ninguém acertou as seis dezenas.
articles.summary: Mega-Sena 3087 teve 18 ganhadores da quadra em Sergipe, com prêmios em Aracaju e interior, enquanto o valor principal acumulou para R$ 40 milhões.
articles.body:
Dezoito apostas de Sergipe acertaram quatro números e ganharam entre R$ 593,12 e R$ 593,15 no concurso 3.087 da Mega-Sena, realizado na noite desta terça-feira (17).

articles.title: Can investment revive South Africa’s economy?
articles.summary: South Africa seeks billions in new investment to revive weak growth and tackle unemployment crisis.
articles.body:
Africa’s most industrialised economy faces an unemployment crisis.

And last year, more foreign investment left South Africa than came in.

Years of power shortages, crumbling infrastructure and corruption have shaken confidence.

One estimate says South Africa needs an additional $75bn a year to revive growth.

President Cyril Ramaphosa is courting US tech giants to help make South Africa an AI hub.

But Washington has hit South Africa with steep tariffs and is cutting its duty-free access to the US market.

Pretoria is increasingly looking to China.

So, can South Africa win back investors and turn promises into jobs?

articles.title: Boato de 'apagão mundial' e onda de ataques hackers: o que aconteceu no mundo nas últimas semanas | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão que circulou nas redes sociais para 17 de novembro não se confirmou. Linha do tempo relembra o roubo bilionário na Binance, a pane da Microsoft e os alertas de autoridades no Brasil e nos EUA.
articles.summary: Previsão que circulou nas redes sociais para 17 de novembro não se confirmou. Linha do tempo relembra o roubo bilionário na Binance, a pane da Microsoft e os alertas de autoridades no Brasil e nos EUA.
articles.body:
Boato de 'apagão mundial' e onda de ataques hackers: o que aconteceu no mundo nas últimas semanas — Foto: Reuters/Divulgação/Reprodução

O mundo, de novo, não acabou. Mas a previsão de um "apagão mundial" dominou as redes sociais na terça-feira (17) , em meio a uma onda de ataques hackers que, desde outubro, atinge de geladeiras de supermercados a bancos.

Só no Brasil, houve casos envolvendo a Caixa Vida e Previdência, a Petrobras, o Porto de Santos e o Tesouro Nacional. E, na mesma terça em que se falava em apagão nas redes, veio a público um ataque a quase 200 sites , entre eles os da BBC, da IKEA e da Air France.

Além dos ataques, houve falhas e alertas que chamaram a atenção no mesmo período. No dia 8, a Defesa Civil Nacional divulgou orientações para montar um kit de emergência . Cinco dias depois, uma falha suspendeu decolagens em todos os aeroportos dos EUA .

Ainda ontem, emissoras de rádio e TV dos EUA interromperam a programação para transmitir uma mensagem do Sistema de Alerta de Emergência (EAS, na sigla em inglês).

Relembre, a seguir, o que aconteceu nas últimas semanas...

🧊 12 de outubro: geladeiras de supermercados chegam a 50 °C na França

Durante a noite, hackers elevaram a temperatura de refrigeradores de supermercados franceses a 50 °C. O ataque provocou incêndios e perdas de alimentos em centenas de lojas pelo país.

A Procuradoria de Paris classificou o ataque como de “grande escala” e disse que ele atingiu refrigeradores conectados de várias redes de supermercados. Nas semanas seguintes, o mesmo problema também atingiu Suécia, Irlanda, Holanda, Estônia, Finlândia, Bélgica e Luxemburgo.

🪙 29 e 30 de outubro: Binance anuncia roubo bilionário

Em cerca de 20 minutos, hackers roubaram US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões) da Binance, a maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo. O ataque ocorreu na quinta-feira (29) e foi divulgado pela empresa no dia seguinte.

Segundo especialistas, foi a maior ação criminosa já registrada no setor de criptomoedas.

🦹 5 de novembro: banco francês revela ataque hacker

O banco regional francês Crédit Mutuel Arkéa informou que foi alvo de um ataque hacker. O valor envolvido foi estimado em 100 milhões de euros (cerca de R$ 615 milhões).

Os ataques ao banco francês e à Binance não têm relação.

👨‍💻 12 e 13 de novembro: pane da Microsoft afeta dezenas de países

Quem usa Outlook, Teams ou Copilot no trabalho enfrentou instabilidade entre quinta-feira (12) e sexta-feira (13). A falha global da Microsoft também afetou empresas, governos e serviços de emergência em dezenas de países.

A Microsoft descartou a hipótese de ataque hacker.

🫆16 e 17 de novembro: ataque hacker atinge quase 200 sites

Revelado pelo pesquisador Scott Helme no dia 16, o ataque atingiu cerca de 178 páginas, segundo o site Cybernews. Entre os alvos estavam BBC, IKEA e Air France. Os hackers inseriram código malicioso em ferramentas da plataforma Optimizely para roubar dados de cartões de crédito e informações sobre criptomoedas, além de infectar dispositivos da Apple.

Segundo Helme, as carteiras dos invasores receberam cerca de US$ 7 mil (R$ 40 mil). A Optimizely disse que conteve o ataque e avisou os clientes afetados.

articles.title: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
articles.summary: Putin says Western powers are ‘former hegemons’, with Europe in the midst of a ‘humiliating decline’.
articles.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that Beijing and Moscow should “lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world” following a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit .

Xi and Putin held bilateral discussions on Wednesday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Following Xi, Putin took to the stage, telling the summit that Western powers were “former hegemons”, adding that Europe was in the midst of a “humiliating decline”.

“Experience has shown that the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having lost much of their intimidating power,” Putin said.

“While sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth – let alone crushing the economies of competitors.”

Russia’s economy has been heavily sanctioned by the US and Europe because of its war against Ukraine, which began in February 2022 when Moscow invaded its neighbour.

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Shenzhen, said that both Xi and Putin called for a “more fair and multipolar world order and that the two leaders also said they would maintain close ties amid what they both described as global uncertainty”.

She added that Xi and Putin “have a close personal relationship, and they have met more than 40 times over the years, and these two countries are also strategically aligned”, with China remaining Russia’s biggest trading partner, and Russia providing Beijing with much-needed energy resources.

“Putin clearly took a swing at European countries, in particular, that have put sanctions on Russia,” Yu added.

But in Shenzhen, “Putin is having a bit of a moment in the sun” at the APEC summit, where he is being treated as a guest of honour.

Robert Kelly, a professor of political science at Pusan National University in South Korea’s Busan, said that all three leaders are “coming in with fairly different expectations and desires of what they want”.

“That’s going to make it quite difficult for them to actually find an agreement,” he said. “Nuclear weapons is an area where the three leaders could really make some great progress,” he argued, adding that the current “tripolar world of nuclear powers is different than the Cold War”.

“It would be great if the three of them could actually bring [the arms race] under control,” Kelly told Al Jazeera.

“But all the different parties are in different places – for the Russians, their weapons are very important to bolster their perception as a great power, despite their problems in Ukraine,” he noted.

“The Chinese have engaged in a major buildup, and it doesn’t look like they want arms control, nuclear weapons at least in their 10 years; and the United States has been sort of very standoffish about any kind of deal,” Kelly said.

“There’s a very strong public goods argument for a positive outcome, for an arms control agreement, but it just won’t happen,” he added.

APEC was established in 1989 and has 21 members, accounting for more than 50 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and representing about 2.7 billion people.

The organisation aims to support economic growth and prosperity in the Asia Pacific region.

Leaders are expected to discuss a range of important issues at this year’s summit, including artificial intelligence (AI) and trade – two areas in which the US and China play dominant roles.

A key issue for APEC members and the wider world is the trade truce between Washington and Beijing, and whether it will be extended beyond January.

articles.title: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has an update on 'house tax' that reportedly made Google founder Sergey Brin exit city
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani recently shared an update on the pied-à-terre surcharge, popularly called as 'house tax'.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani recently shared an update on the pied-à-terre surcharge, popularly called as 'house tax'. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Zohran Mamdani said that the city has billed over $500 million to rich owners of second homes. “That’s half a billion dollars to invest in a City that works for all New Yorkers,” Mamdani wrote. Introduced earlier this year, the pied-à-terre tax apples to homes worth over $5 million that are not the owner’s main residence. Among those impacted by the tax includes Google founder Sergey Brin, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Dell CEO Michael Dell. A Bloomberg report in July said that Sergey Brin walked away from a sizable bet on New York City apartment, selling his stake in a struggling real estate fund for just six cents on the dollar.Here’s the update on ‘house tax’ that Zohran Mamdani sharedSharing the X post, Zohran Mamdani wrote:“An update on our pied-à-terre surcharge: We’ve billed more than $500 million to owners of second homes worth more than $5 million. That’s half a billion dollars to invest in a City that works for all New Yorkers”.What is Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax and which properties are coveredAs mentioned above, the new pied-à-terre tax is a surcharge on houses that are not the primary residence of owners. It applies to one-, two- and three-family homes valued at more than $5 million, as well as condominiums and co-ops valued at $1 million or more, if those properties are not a person's primary residence.The measure is intended primarily to cover owners who maintain homes in New York City while living elsewhere for most of the year and therefore do not pay New York City income taxes.Why Sergey Brin 'exited' New York CityAccording to a Bloomberg report, Google founder Sergey Brin offloaded his sizable holding in a New York City apartment back to the fund's manager, A&E Real Estate. Amphitheatre LLC, an entity tied to Brin, sold its shares in a fund holding nearly 5,900 units across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx, the report stated. Many of those apartments fall under New York's rent-stabilization program.A&E then confirmed the buyout without naming Brin, saying the investor "was willing to accept six cents on the dollar on their original equity investment to divest itself from the New York City multifamily sector.”Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: Devon blue brook pollution focus of resident survey
articles.summary: The Environment Agency wants to know how the incident affected visitors, residents and businesses.
articles.body:
People affected by a pollution incident that turned a brook bright blue are being asked to share their experiences as part of an ongoing investigation.

The Environment Agency has launched a survey following the contamination of Littleham Brook in Exmouth, Devon between 11 and 25 September .

It prompted warnings against swimming and other water activities at Exmouth beach while officials investigated the cause.

Clarissa Newell, regulatory manager at the Environment Agency, said: "We want information from people, businesses and organisations who may have been affected by this incident.

"This could be specifically during this period or you may still be experiencing ongoing impacts."

The Environment Agency said the anonymous feedback could help investigators understand the wider effects of the pollution and may lead to witness statements supporting the inquiry.

It said possible impacts included illness, cancelled water activities, disrupted visits and reduced income for businesses.

No information could be shared at this stage on the source of the pollution as it could affect any future legal action, it added.

Paper copies of the survey are available from Exmouth Town Hall.

articles.title: ‘We want to go back’: Rohingya refugees pin hopes on ICJ genocide verdict
articles.summary: After almost a decade in exile, they’re hoping the ICJ rules in their favour. But will that help them get back home?
articles.body:
Cox’s Bazar/Dhaka, Bangladesh — When Dil Hossain and his wife, Alinnesa, fled Myanmar’s Rakhine State during the military crackdown on their Rohingya community in 2017, they carried their newborn daughter, Ishara, and ran for their lives.

Dil’s elderly parents could not escape and were killed as the family fled, along with several other relatives.

“We ran for our lives through mud, hills and water, with the baby tied to us,” Alinnesa recalls.

Nearly nine years later, Ishara is growing up in a refugee camp in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, far from the village where she was born. She has spent almost her entire life in exile. Her parents depend on humanitarian aid, which has declined sharply in recent years, and continue to wait for a chance to return home.

Now, the family is hoping the International Court of Justice (ICJ) will recognise the atrocities committed against the Rohingya. On Thursday, the highest court of the United Nations is due to deliver its judgement in a landmark genocide case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar.

The Gambia filed the case on November 11, 2019, alleging that Myanmar had violated the 1948 Genocide Convention through acts committed against the Rohingya by its military and other security forces.

The allegations concern the so-called “clearance operations” that began in 2016 and escalated in August 2017, which The Gambia says involved genocidal acts intended to destroy the Rohingya, in whole or in part. The case asks the ICJ to determine Myanmar’s responsibility as a state under the convention.

“The court will find the truth. We suffered, so we know,” Dil said, expressing confidence that the judges would recognise the atrocities committed against the Rohingya.

More than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees remain in Bangladesh, most of them in camps in Cox’s Bazar. Many hope a ruling in their favour will bring recognition of their suffering and strengthen their claim to return home.

But even a landmark legal judgement in their favour may do little to change their lives immediately. Myanmar remains engulfed in civil war, with the same military that committed crimes against the Rohingya still in power, so the prospects for a safe return remain remote.

A life of ’24 hours of depression’ in exile

For many Rohingya refugees, nearly nine years in Bangladesh have brought a different kind of hardship: dependence on aid, uncertainty and a life far removed from the homes they left behind.

Nurul Amin, 25, who works with humanitarian groups in the camps, said the contrast between his former life in Myanmar and his present circumstances was stark.

“Back home, we had houses, big trees, gardens and farmland. We could grow our own food and did not have to depend on others. We were self-sufficient,” he said. “Here, we have to depend on others for almost everything. The difference is like that between heaven and earth.”

Years of displacement have also taken a toll on his mental wellbeing, he said. “It is 24 hours of depression. It feels as though we have lost our world, as though the world has abandoned us.”

Mohammad Rehan, now 18, was a child when the military crackdown began, but retains vivid memories that he says have left a lifelong mark.

“The most horrific thing I saw was houses being burned. It made me really afraid,” he said. “I was very young at the time, and those scenes left me traumatised.”

He hopes the court will recognise the Rohingya’s suffering and their right to equal treatment.

“If they find Myanmar guilty, I think it will help our community return and reclaim our rights,” he said.

The case brought by The Gambia accuses Myanmar of violating its obligations under the convention through the military’s treatment of the Rohingya, particularly during the 2017 crackdown.

For Rohingya leaders and activists, the ruling is more about whether the court recognises the crimes as genocide. They want their identity and rights restored, and those responsible held accountable.

Mohammad Zubair, chairman of the Arakan Rohingya Society for Peace and Human Rights, said the community was confident the court would recognise what it had endured.

“They called us Bengali and committed genocide on us,” he said, referring to Myanmar’s refusal to even recognise the Rohingya as a community. “We witnessed the genocide with our own eyes. We suffered it. There has been enough evidence and testimony.”

Zubair said a favourable judgement could help pave the way for their return to Myanmar with dignity and rights. “The refugee life is worse than jail. There is no hope, and this is unbearable,” he said. “I have been a teacher for about two decades and was widely respected in Myanmar. Now I am living a refugee life. We want to go back.”

Nay San Lwin, a Rohingya activist and cofounder of the Free Rohingya Coalition, said meaningful justice would need more than just a court ruling.

“For us, meaningful justice is not simply a court verdict,” he said. “It means recognition of our identity, restoration of our rights, justice for every victim, and the opportunity to return to our homeland safely, rebuild our lives, and live in peace and dignity.”

That would require guarantees of citizenship, equal rights and recognition of the Rohingya as an ethnic community, he said. Refugees must also be able to return to their original villages and enjoy the same rights as other communities in Myanmar.

“If the court recognises that genocide took place against the Rohingya, the international community, including the United Nations, must ensure that the judgement is implemented without delay and that those responsible are held accountable,” Nay San Lwin said.

But even if the court does not find Myanmar responsible for genocide, he added, the struggle for justice would continue.

“Such a judgement would not erase our suffering or eliminate the need for accountability. Our commitment to justice does not depend on a single verdict,” Nay San Lwin said.

The judgement could have implications well beyond the Rohingya community.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for genocide. A ruling against Myanmar would therefore carry major implications for international law, said Michael Kugelman, a resident senior fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic Council.

It would also have consequences for Bangladesh, which has hosted the world’s largest Rohingya refugee population for years, he said. “If the court rules that the Rohingya were a victim of genocide, there will likely be ample pressure on Dhaka to provide more support and protections for Rohingya on their soil,” Kugelman said. “If the court doesn’t make this call, the pressure wouldn’t be as great.”

Nasir Uddin, a professor of anthropology at the University of Chittagong who has written extensively on the community, said a favourable judgement would formally recognise the atrocities committed against the Rohingya in 2017 within an international legal framework.

It would also give the community’s political demands a stronger legal basis, he said.

“The Rohingya crisis is often treated as a political bargaining issue. But once the court holds Myanmar accountable for genocide, those demands would have a stronger legal foundation,” he said. “There is a difference between making a political speech and having a legal judgement supporting your claims.”

The case could also reinforce the principle that countries not directly affected by atrocities can still bring a case under the Genocide Convention. The Gambia was not involved in the events in Myanmar, but brought the case before the court.

A ruling against Myanmar could therefore have implications for future cases involving alleged genocide elsewhere, Uddin said.

But he cautioned that the legal threshold for proving genocide is high. The court must establish that there was specific intent to destroy a protected group, in whole or in part. Myanmar has argued that its 2017 operations were counterinsurgency measures.

“I would not necessarily expect an entirely black-and-white judgement,” Uddin said. “The court may recognise some aspects of the case while subjecting others to legal scrutiny.”

A ruling that does not recognise the genocide allegation, he added, could strengthen what he calls the “politics of denial” and undermine confidence in international justice.

“I fear that genocide denial is now prevailing over the recognition of genocide around the world. This will give future atrocities a sense of impunity.”

Kugelman said a genocide finding could increase calls in the international community for further legal action against Myanmar’s military authorities. But he warned that the response from the country’s neighbours was likely to be more limited.

“As dramatic as a genocide verdict would be, Myanmar’s neighbours would likely continue to take a pragmatic position,” Kugelman said. “And of course this would redound to the regime’s benefit.”

Even a favourable ICJ judgement would not guarantee the Rohingya a safe return to Myanmar.

The country’s civil war has transformed the balance of power in Rakhine State. The Arakan Army, a rebel group, has taken control of nearly all the state, including northern areas from which many Rohingya refugees fled.

Thomas Kean of the International Crisis Group said the group would be a necessary partner in any future repatriation discussions.

But relations between the Arakan Army and Rohingya communities have been badly damaged by the conflict, he said. In 2024, Rohingya armed groups fought alongside Myanmar’s military against the Arakan Army, while the military also conscripted Rohingya into militias. The Arakan Army has since been accused of abuses against Rohingya civilians, while Rohingya armed groups have carried out attacks in northern Rakhine.

“This violence has significantly undermined trust between the Rohingya, many of whom see the Arakan Army as equivalent [to], if not worse than, the Myanmar military, and the Arakan Army, which views the Rohingya as a potential security threat,” Kean said. “Lack of trust between the two sides is a major barrier to repatriation, and it could take years of patient work to improve the relationship.”

The ongoing fighting makes a return even more difficult, he said.

“The Arakan Army can hardly make guarantees around safety while a war is going on,” Kean said. “An end to the conflict in Rakhine would be the first step towards repatriation, but there would still be a long road ahead to making it happen.”

Kean also doubts how much additional leverage a genocide ruling would give the international community, when it comes to pressuring Myanmar’s military government.

Myanmar’s authorities have said they are willing to allow the Rohingya to return when security conditions permit. They have also indicated a willingness to grant citizenship, provided the refugees do not insist on being recognised as Rohingya.

He warned that a finding of genocide could instead make Myanmar’s military authorities more resistant to international pressure and lead to further restrictions on the work of the UN and other international organisations.

“I also fear that a genocide finding against Myanmar would only make Naypyidaw more recalcitrant,” he said, referring to Myanmar’s administrative capital. “I think there’s also a risk of a broader backlash within Myanmar, or among Myanmar people, many of whom likely still see the Rohingya as illegal immigrants.”

That concern also finds an echo among Rohingya refugees. Rohingya youth Nurul Amin said a favourable judgement should not be seen as a victory for the community alone.

“There are many other ethnic communities in Myanmar that are also under attack. We want them to live in peace, with democracy restored, and to coexist,” he said. “We want justice and our rights back. But we also want all the ethnic communities in Myanmar to be able to live peacefully, without fear of the military.”

Nasir Uddin said the judgement could provide legal recognition and generate international pressure on Myanmar. But it could not itself bring the refugees home.

“We should not assume that a favourable ICJ judgement means the Rohingya will return home the next day,” he said. “These things take time. Nothing will change overnight.”

Kean said Bangladesh would also need to engage with the different actors in Myanmar’s conflict rather than rely on one side alone. Dhaka should establish a channel for sustained dialogue with the Arakan Army, particularly on repatriation, border security, trade and humanitarian assistance, he said.

For Dil and Alinnesa, however, the question is more immediate. Will their daughter ever have the chance to grow up in the country where she was born, with the rights and security her parents lost?

“We have lost our lives, our properties and our people,” Alinnesa said. “The refugee life we are living here has no future for us and our kids. We want to return to our homes and live our lives in peace.”

articles.title: David Lammy urges Andy Burnham to take UK back into the EU
articles.summary: The former deputy PM's intervention comes after Burnham reopened a debate over the UK's long-term future.
articles.body:
David Lammy has urged Andy Burnham to take Labour into the next general election with a pledge to rejoin the European Union.

The former deputy prime minister's intervention comes as Burnham prepares to reopen a debate on the long-term relationship with Europe in the wake of a summit in Brussels this Friday.

It makes him the latest senior Labour figure to publicly support a future reversal of Brexit, after ex-chancellor Rachel Reeves said she believed Britain's future lies in the bloc.

Burnham confirmed on Tuesday he plans to set out options for a future relationship next month, alongside his blueprint to boost the British economy over the next decade.

The prime minister has held out the possibility he could ask to rejoin at some stage, whilst ruling out major changes before the next election.

In an article earlier this month, Reeves said she believed "Britain's future lies in the European Union", without specifying a timeframe for the move and insisting it was important to "get the next steps right".

But Lammy has now gone further, calling for Burnham to advocate rejoining at the next election, paving the way for a negotiation on a deal to return.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, he added that the public should then be given a vote on whether to accept the new membership deal.

Returning to the bloc's customs union, in which EU member states charge the same taxes on imported goods, would not deliver "enough" economic growth, he said.

He added that rejoining Europe's single market from the outside was "not a runner" as it would mean applying swathes of EU law without a say on the content.

Another cabinet minister under Sir Keir Starmer, Peter Kyle, has also backed this approach, writing on Substack that a "complex halfway option" would be "the worst of all worlds".

He added that a promise to rejoin at the next election, followed by a renegotiation and a referendum on the final terms, was the "only way through I see".

He added: "How would I vote? Well, I would want to see the deal before deciding. I want Britain back in the EU, but not at any cost."

Burnham to set out options next month for long-term EU relationship

The EU that Burnham is eyeing up is very different to the one Britain left

Lammy, who is also a former foreign secretary, argued the UK would be able to rejoin the EU whilst staying outside the passport-free Schengen travel zone and without committing to adopt the euro.

But he appeared to concede that Britain's EU budget rebate, first negotiated in the 1980s, could become less financially generous, adding that a "different formula" for financial contributions would be "up for negotiation".

He also revealed he had made an unsuccessful attempt to persuade Sir Keir to "tear up" his red lines on Europe towards the end of his two-year premiership, but the former prime minister had encountered resistance from within his cabinet.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto committed the party to "make Brexit work" whilst ruling out rejoining either its customs union or single market.

Any move away from those red lines by Burnham would set up a huge dividing line with the Conservatives and Reform UK at the next election.

But Lammy argued the prime minister's status as a former mayor from the north of England meant he was "uniquely placed" to convince the public of the need to reverse the decision to leave.

It comes as Burnham prepares to travel to the Brussels this Friday for an EU summit at which both sides hope to unveil new agreements on food, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.

The prime minister inherited negotiations on those deals from his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, who kicked off talks on the agreements last year.

But he has also started a broader discussion over the UK's long-term relationship with Europe, which has been welcomed by some within his own party but seen him accused by critics of betraying the result of the 2016 decision to leave.

Burnham's Conservative predecessor Lord Cameron, who resigned as prime minister after losing the 2016 Brexit referendum, has urged the Labour leader not to start a renewed debate over EU membership.

Speaking last week, he warned a fresh debate over the issue would be "long and painful" and could harm attempts to improve upon the exit deal negotiated under the Conservatives.

He added: "The EU countries will just think: 'Well, these guys are gonna rejoin anyway, so what's the point in giving them a good partnership deal'."

articles.title: Burst pipe leaves 8,500 properties without water in Stourbridge
articles.summary: Residents have been unable to cook, wash or flush their toilets since Tuesday afternoon.
articles.body:
Thousands of properties across Stourbridge, in the West Midlands, remain without water on Wednesday as teams work to locate a burst pipe, with repairs potentially taking until the weekend.

Ridgewood High School and Ashwood Park Primary School remained closed, and residents said they had been unable to cook, wash or flush their toilets.

Emergency bottled water stations have been operating since 08:00 GMT, although supplies temporarily ran out at one site before a fresh delivery was arranged.

Severn Trent said bottled water would be available until 22:00 on Wednesday and every day until supplies were restored, but warned the complex repair could take several more days.

On Wednesday morning, it was reported that 6,000 homes and businesses were without water, but by lunchtime that had risen to 8,500 as engineers attempted to find the source of the leak.

Howard Perry, head of water quality at Severn Trent said some residents could be without water for four days.

"We are very hopeful we can get customers back on supply before that," he said.

One resident said she had a three-week-old baby and was concerned when supplies of bottled water temporarily ran out.

She said she used a two-and-a-half-litre bottle just to clean and sterilise baby bottles.

"They've delivered water to the vulnerable, and they've been pinched, people are taking it off the doorstep," she added.

Emergency bottled water stations have been set up at Sainsbury's car park on Sandringham Way in Amblecote and at King George V Park on Lawnswood Road in Wordsley.

The scale of the disruption was clear at the site in Amblecote, where residents queued for bottled water.

Customers were allowed to take up to 24 litres of water each, but the limit was later reduced to 12 litres per person as demand increased.

There was a constant stream of residents arriving throughout Wednesday morning.

Motorists faced lengthy delays just to reach the distribution point.

One resident said it took about 40 minutes to get close enough to turn into the Sainsbury's car park, leading some drivers to abandon their cars on nearby residential streets and continue on foot.

One resident caring for young children said the lack of updates from the water supplier were concerning.

"We've had no updates from Severn Trent at all about what's going on," she said.

"I've got two children and we've got no water today at the moment at all.

"You turn your taps on, nothing comes out."

At the water station, residents expressed mixed views about the response to the water supply problems.

Some praised Severn Trent staff, saying crews worked hard in difficult conditions to restore supplies and support affected communities.

Others questioned whether the amount of water being distributed would be sufficient, particularly if repairs continued into a second day. There were also concerns about how long supplies at the distribution point would last.

Keith Hunter said the situation had left him unable to "cook dinner or flush my toilet".

"These companies charge more and more money every year, but the service doesn't get better."

Resident Chris Clinton doubted the six two-litre bottles of water would last until the issue was resolved.

"This is horrendous because there's no water at all, so you can't wash. You can't put anything on or do anything, it's just terrible," he said.

"For the amount of people that it affects, that's just not going to be good enough.

"They need tankers, people need to have a water supply."

Marion Thompson said the closed schools and queuing for water made her think of the early Covid-19 pandemic.

"The school by us is shut again so kids can't go to school, so it's like everything's happening at the same time."

articles.title: Amid string of outages, bipartisan letter urges strategy to combat AI-assisted cyber threats
articles.summary: In the midst of a series of recent cyber outages, there is growing concern by members of Congress that the Trump administration needs to do more to protect infrastructure from cyberattacks that are aided by AI, according to a new bipartisan letter sent by two senators to the White House’s AI czar.
articles.body: In the midst of a series of recent cyber outages, there is growing concern by members of Congress that the Trump administration needs to do more to protect infrastructure from cyberattacks that are aided by AI, according to a new bipartisan letter sent by two senators to the White House’s AI czar. The letter from U.S. Sens. Maria Cantwell from Washington state, the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee, and Mike Rounds, the Republican from South Dakota who chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, urges AI czar Jay Clayton to develop a new national strategy that addresses AI-assisted cyber threats. “AI is rapidly increasing the ability to discover and exploit weaknesses in software, and our defenses are not keeping pace,” the senators wrote. They noted that AI can quickly find vulnerabilities in software and get around regular cyber defenses. Repair patches that are supposed to protect infrastructure can take weeks or months to test and install. And they wrote that autonomous AI agents can introduce new security risks. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday. It’s not clear what kind of role, if any, AI has played in the ongoing outages impacting U.S. consumers and travelers, but questions are expected to come up when Clayton testifies before the House Committee on Homeland Security on Wednesday morning. Clayton who also serves as the Director of National Intelligence was named to the AI role in early October is leading a task force of government officials to produce an AI policy by the end of January. In their letter to Clayton, the senators cited an ongoing wave of cyberattacks in Japan that have impacted financial institutions and companies, leading “to large-scale data breaches and leaks, which the Japanese government is now seeking to contain.” The string of attacks are believed to be boosted by AI. They also pointed to incidents where rogue artificial intelligence agents have accessed customers’ bank accounts, leaving banks worried that AI could initiate transactions on its own. The senators are asking for Clayton’s task force to bring together AI companies and federal agencies to secure digital infrastructure and develop security standards for autonomous AI agents. Speaking to reporters in the Philippines overnight, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sought to reassure Americans, saying that recent outages such as those that impacted Microsoft Outlook, United Airlines and the Federal Aviation Administration are not connected to one another. “We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” he said.

articles.title: Florida man grabs invasive python in Everglades National Park thinking he is protecting wildlife, gets $180 fine and ranger warnings; his legal battle ends with the citation being dropped
articles.summary: A trip through Everglades National Park took an unexpected turn for Yatir Nitzany when he came across an invasive Burmese python and decided to catch it
articles.body: A trip through Everglades National Park took an unexpected turn for Yatir Nitzany when he came across an invasive Burmese python and decided to catch it himself. The encounter, which was recorded on camera, later brought him into conflict with federal park regulations. Although Florida authorities have encouraged efforts to remove invasive species, handling wildlife inside a national park comes with different restrictions. According to NBC6 South Florida, Nitzany received a $180 citation from a park ranger for taking hold of the snake. Months of uncertainty over the penalty eventually led him to federal court, where the case was dismissed on Friday. The decision, however, left him without a clear explanation of why the citation had been withdrawn.The growing problem of Burmese pythons in the EvergladesNitzany said he had not set out on a dedicated python-hunting trip when he encountered the snake. It crossed his path during his visit to Everglades National Park, prompting him to intervene. He argued that Burmese pythons pose a serious threat to the area's wildlife and that removing one from the environment was the right thing to do.The invasive snakes have become a major concern in South Florida, where their presence has affected native animal populations. Burmese pythons are non-native predators that feed on a wide range of mammals and birds. Their ability to establish themselves in the Everglades has made controlling their numbers a continuing challenge for wildlife authorities.Speaking about his decision to grab the animal, Nitzany pointed to the damage he believed the species was causing. He said the snakes had become dominant predators in the ecosystem, affecting the natural balance between native species.The $180 fine that sparked a legal disputeNitzany's attempt to handle the python brought him into contact with federal park regulations. A ranger issued him a citation carrying a $180 penalty for handling wildlife on federal land without authorisation.The distinction between removing an invasive animal and handling wildlife inside a national park became central to the dispute. Florida has programmes that allow trained participants and members of the public to help remove invasive pythons from designated areas. Those arrangements do not automatically extend to national parks, where separate federal rules govern interactions with wildlife.Nitzany disputed the penalty, saying he did not believe his actions amounted to wrongdoing. He questioned why someone attempting to remove an invasive species should face a fine, particularly when the animal was considered harmful to the surrounding environment.Wildlife advocate Ron Magill joined him in courtWhen the matter reached federal court, Nitzany was accompanied by wildlife advocate Ron Magill. The two were prepared to challenge the citation and explain the environmental problems associated with Burmese pythons in the Everglades.The hearing ended with the citation being dismissed. However, Nitzany said he and Magill were not given a detailed account of the grounds for the decision. According to Nitzany, they were simply told that the citation had been written incorrectly.The dismissal brought an end to the immediate dispute over the $180 penalty, but it did not settle the wider question of whether members of the public should be allowed to intervene when they encounter invasive species inside federal parks.Nitzany recounts ranger warnings ahead of federal court hearingNitzany also described receiving text messages and voicemail recordings from park rangers during the period before the court appearance. He said the communications made him uncomfortable, particularly because they referred to the possibility of a federal bench warrant if he failed to appear.In one recorded message, a ranger warned that the matter could be taken before a judge and that a warrant might be requested if Nitzany did not attend court. He interpreted the warning as pressure to settle the citation by paying the fine.Asked whether the communication had felt threatening, Nitzany said he was concerned by the possibility of facing further legal consequences over a penalty he believed was unjustified. The issue became another part of his account of how the citation had been handled.Wildlife advocate wants exception for removing invasive pythonsMagill said the case had drawn attention to a difference between Florida's approach to invasive species and the restrictions operating on federal land. While state-level initiatives encourage the removal of Burmese pythons in authorised circumstances, national park regulations place limits on what visitors can do when they encounter wildlife. He said he wanted to push for a change that would allow an exception for people attempting to remove invasive animals, rather than penalising them for intervening. His proposed change would need to account for the particular rules governing national parks and ensure that any removal activity could be carried out safely and appropriately.The National Park Service and the US Attorney's Office were contacted by NBC6 for comment. The broadcaster sought clarification about the reason for the dismissal and whether park rangers routinely contact people who receive citations. Neither office had responded at the time of its report. For Nitzany, the court's decision meant he no longer had to contest the $180 penalty. The broader disagreement over how visitors should respond to invasive pythons on federal land, however, remained unresolved.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger bought the M47 Patton tank he once drove during Austrian military service; the 46-tonne Cold War vehicle later became part of his Hollywood life and even featured in a Netflix stunt
articles.summary: Hollywood actor Arnold Schwarzenegger owns an unusual reminder of his early years, a 46-tonne M47 Patton tank that he once operated during compulsory
articles.body: Hollywood actor Arnold Schwarzenegger owns an unusual reminder of his early years, a 46-tonne M47 Patton tank that he once operated during compulsory military service in Austria. The actor served as a tank driver at the Belgier barracks in Graz between 1965 and 1966, when he was 18. Decades later, he purchased the same military vehicle from the Austrian armed forces and brought it to the US. The Cold War-era tank subsequently became part of his public persona and attracted attention through his association with it. In 2023, Schwarzenegger even drove the vehicle over a Mercedes-Benz in a Netflix promotional stunt, using his personal tank for the announcement of his role as the streaming platform's Chief Action Officer.Arnold Schwarzenegger served as an M47 tank driver in AustriaSchwarzenegger completed his compulsory military service in the Austrian armed forces between October 1965 and June 1966. According to the Austrian Ministry of Defence, he was stationed at the Belgier barracks in Graz, where he served as a driver of an M47 Patton tank.During his service, Schwarzenegger also experienced an unusual accident involving the vehicle. Recalling the incident during a visit to his former barracks in August 2012, he explained that he had been conducting a routine check on the tank when he failed to notice that it was in reverse gear.The vehicle consequently moved backwards through the brick wall of a garage. Schwarzenegger later recalled the incident as a small accident from his military days.The Austrian Ministry of Defence confirmed that he eventually purchased his former tank from the armed forces in 1994.Austrian Army dug up and restored the tank for himThe story behind how Schwarzenegger recovered his former military vehicle is unusual. After his military service ended, the Austrian Army had buried the tank as part of a decommissioning process.According to Netflix Tudum, Schwarzenegger later contacted the Austrian military and expressed his interest in acquiring the vehicle. The army subsequently dug it up, restored it and transferred it to him.He eventually brought the tank from Austria to the US, where it remained part of his personal collection.Schwarzenegger has also spoken about using the tank's storage space to keep weights and dumbbells during his military service. He would work out between drills, continuing his bodybuilding training even while serving in the army.Schwarzenegger drove his personal tank over a Mercedes-Benz for NetflixIn May 2023, Schwarzenegger brought his M47 Patton tank into the spotlight through a promotional video announcing his appointment as Netflix's Chief Action Officer.The video showed the actor driving the 46-tonne military vehicle over a Mercedes-Benz outside Netflix's offices. The stunt was part of the streaming platform's promotional campaign for its 2023 action-film and television lineup.In an interview with Netflix Tudum, Schwarzenegger confirmed that he personally operated the tank rather than allowing a stunt driver to take control."Was it really me driving? Of course it was. I wasn't going to let someone else have that fun," he said.The stunt reportedly took just two takes, with the tank crushing two different cars during filming. A stunt team that had worked with Schwarzenegger for around 30 years supported the production.He explained that he was particularly keen to use his personal M47 because it was the exact same tank he had driven as an 18-year-old in the Austrian Army.What is the M47 Patton tank?The M47 Patton was an American medium tank developed during the early years of the Cold War. Its development accelerated following the outbreak of the Korean War in 1950, when the US Army sought a more capable armoured vehicle to counter newer Soviet tanks.The vehicle was developed by combining a modified turret from the T42 tank with the existing hull of the M46 Patton. It was equipped with a 90mm main gun and a stereoscopic rangefinder designed to improve targeting accuracy.According to The Tank Museum, production of the M47 ran from July 1951 to November 1953, with 8,576 units manufactured by the American Locomotive Company and the Detroit Tank Arsenal.The tank weighed approximately 46 tonnes and was powered by an 810-horsepower, 12-cylinder petrol engine. It could reach speeds of up to 30 mph (48 km/h) on suitable terrain and had an operating range of approximately 80 miles.It required a crew of five, including a driver, assistant driver, gunner, loader and commander.M47 Patton was used by several countries during the Cold WarAlthough the M47's service with the US military was relatively short, the vehicle continued operating in several countries after being supplied to American allies.The US Army began replacing it with the M48 Patton from 1953, and the M47 was declared obsolete in 1957. However, several countries continued using the tank for decades.Its international operators included Austria, Belgium, France, Italy, Pakistan, South Korea, Turkey, Iran and West Germany.The vehicle also saw combat in several conflicts, including the 1965 India-Pakistan War, the 1967 Six-Day War and the Iran-Iraq War of 1980-88.According to The Tank Museum, Pakistan deployed M47 tanks against Indian forces during the 1965 conflict, including in the major armoured battles at Asal Uttar and Chawinda.Schwarzenegger uses the tank to raise money for charityBeyond its military history and Hollywood appearances, Schwarzenegger's M47 has also been used to support charitable causes.Netflix reported that the actor uses his personal tank to raise money for charity. The vehicle has become a distinctive part of his public identity, connecting his early military experience with his later career as an actor and public figure.Schwarzenegger has previously spoken about his attachment to the vehicle, particularly because it represents a period when he was balancing compulsory military service with his ambitions in bodybuilding.You use AI every day. articles.title: Xi Jinping greets Trump as he arrives in China, a rare move ahead of talks with Putin
articles.summary: In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
articles.body: SHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China. He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit. Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents. A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington. “China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said. After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags. Xi’s gesture Wednesday most likely reflects a desire by him and his government to “show respect to Trump,” which they know he enjoys, William Yang, a senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, said in a post on X. “It is likely also an attempt to uphold the positive rapport between Xi and Trump ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations in the coming months,” he said. When Trump last visited China in May, he was greeted at the airport in Beijing by Vice President Han Zheng. Putin, who has a close relationship with Xi and has met with him 50 times as of Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader when he arrived earlier at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport. Putin was instead met by Cai Qi, a close Xi adviser and member of the Politburo Standing Committee. Xi has met with a number of world leaders, including Putin, as they gather in Shenzhen this week for a summit of Asia-Pacific economies. Trump, Putin and Xi are holding an unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the summit. Ahead of his bilateral meeting with Xi on Wednesday, Putin said he expected “great potential benefits” from the trilateral talks, which have sparked anxiety in places such as Ukraine, Iran and the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan, where officials worry the world’s three most powerful leaders could make decisions about their futures without consulting them. In a briefing last week, a senior U.S. official said the trilateral meeting was unlikely to produce any sort of agreement, describing it as an “entry point” and “the first conversation.”
