articles.title: What is Iraq’s Jurf al-Sakhar and what is behind gov’t push to control it?
articles.summary: Tensions surge between PM al-Zaidi’s government and Kataib Hezbollah amid oil-smuggling scandal.
articles.body:
Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of Iran-linked fighters in Iraq, has emerged as the focal point of a sweeping anticorruption campaign launched by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government following accusations of oil smuggling.

Located some 60km (37 miles) southwest of Baghdad and spanning roughly 345 square kilometres (133 square miles), the area holds immense strategic significance along the Shia pilgrimage route between the Iraqi capital and the holy city of Karbala.

It was once the site of former President Saddam Hussein’s military-industrial complexes, making its geography ideal for testing, building and concealing weapons.

Following the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003 that toppled Hussein, it became a hotspot for armed confrontations before the ISIL (ISIS) armed group seized it in 2014. Later that year, the Iran-backed Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), an umbrella organisation of mostly Shia armed groups, recaptured the territory from ISIL.

Kataib Hezbollah, one of the largest groups within PMF, subsequently took full control, renaming the area Jurf al-Nasr and barring state institutions from entering. The militia sealed the town, citing security concerns, effectively preventing the return of approximately 140,000 displaced residents.

Last week, a leaked intelligence report said millions of dollars’ worth of crude oil had been siphoned from two state pipelines passing through the closed area since 2021. According to the document prepared by the Iraqi Ministry of Interior, the perpetrators allegedly constructed makeshift underground refineries to process the stolen resources.

The information led al-Zaidi to form a high-level investigative committee that entered the restricted zone on November 13 with military backing to confirm the existence of the illicit facilities. Earlier this week, the committee said it had identified several locations linked to smuggling operations in the area, without naming those allegedly implicated. As part of the anticorruption crackdown, nine senior security and administrative officials in Babil province, including the provincial police chief and the director of the Oil Pipelines Company, have also been dismissed.

According to the state Iraqi News Agency, the government has “ordered the armed forces to enter” Jurf al-Sakhar, setting a deadline “for the armed faction to exit the area”. Reports say the deadline for the withdrawal is Friday.

Kataib Hezbollah has denied the oil-smuggling allegations and, in harshly worded statements, accused al-Zaidi of corruption and framed the crackdown as a political extortion campaign. In a major show of force, the militia also mobilised approximately 8,000 fighters from various provinces towards Jurf al-Sakhar ahead of the government committee’s arrival.

Iraqi writer and journalist Hamza Mustafa told Al Jazeera that the military posturing masks underlying vulnerabilities. “What the brigades are doing through field mobilisation is perhaps the last line of defence for them after their position appeared weak regarding the oil-smuggling operations,” said Mustafa, noting that the previous narrative of fighting “terrorism” no longer held.

Security expert Saif Raad said the militia’s fierce resistance is driven by economics amid allegations that the restricted zone is also used to run thousands of illegal fish farms. “The desperation over this area is not for security reasons but for financial reasons,” said Raad, a former military officer.

Since taking office in May, al-Zaidi has made the disarmament of all armed factions in the country, including Kataib Hezbollah, a priority amid pressure from the United States, which has long demanded the decommissioning of the Iran-backed fighters. An initial September 30, 2026, deadline to bring all weapons under state control has since been pushed to June 2027.

“The issue here comes in the context of removing all pretexts from the armed factions after it was revealed that they are smuggling oil,” said Mustafa.

Fadel Abu Ragheef, an Iraqi political analyst, told Al Jazeera that al-Zaidi is in a distinctive position to take such unprecedented steps against entrenched interests. “He did not come from a partisan or bloc background, so his decisions are characterised by boldness and daring,” argued Abu Ragheef.

The standoff has deeply divided Iraq’s ruling Coordination Framework, prompting leaders such as Nouri al-Maliki, Hadi al-Amiri, Qais al-Khazali and Ammar al-Hakim to frantically mediate behind the scenes. Abu Ragheef suggested these factions are highly sensitive to issues such as disarmament.

“They harden their position if they hear the word disarmament or containment, so the concepts have shifted from disarmament and containment to organisation and management,” said Abu Ragheef, noting that the change has provided a crucial negotiating window until the June 2027 deadline.

With Friday’s deadline looming, Iran has also stepped in to avert a direct military clash. Esmail Qaani, commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, headed to Baghdad to mediate the crisis and push for a solution. Qaani and al-Zaidi reportedly held talks until dawn on Tuesday, reaching a tentative agreement that would see Kataib Hezbollah withdraw “soon”.

Still, Mustafa warned that the crisis is not fully resolved.

“Qaani has not been able to dismantle the scene so far like he used to,” he said, referring to Iran’s historical influence, noting that Tehran had come to realise the issue is larger than expected due to al-Zaidi’s insistence.

Raad echoed this, emphasising al-Zaidi’s determination to centralise state arms, comparing it to his recent successful pacification of armed groups in the Sinjar district.

“The prime minister will not be prevented by Qaani or anyone else from going and restoring the authority of the commander in chief of the armed forces over all Iraqi territories,” he said. “This crisis is a beginning to restore the sovereign decision of the state.”

articles.title: Hindu population growth to fall behind other religions in India, globally: Pew Study
articles.summary: India's Hindu population is projected to increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, but Hindus are expected to account for a slightly smaller share of
articles.body: India's Hindu population is projected to increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, but Hindus are expected to account for a slightly smaller share of the country's population as Muslims continue to have higher fertility rates, according to new projections by the Pew Research Center.Despite the projected shift, Hindus are expected to continue making up more than three-quarters of India's population by 2070.The global Hindu population is also projected to grow by 199 million over the same period, reaching nearly 1.4 billion. However, as the rest of the world's population is expected to grow at a faster pace, Hindus' share of the global population is projected to decline from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.The projections are part of a broader Pew Research Center study examining changes in the size and composition of major religious groups between 2020 and 2070. The estimates take into account differences in fertility rates, age profiles, religious switching and international migration.India's changing religious compositionPew said that although India's overall fertility rate has declined rapidly in recent decades, Muslim women continue to have more children on average than Hindu women. Combined with the younger age profile of India's Muslim population, this fertility gap is expected to increase the Muslim share of the country's population while reducing the Hindu share.India had 1.1 billion Hindus in 2020, accounting for around 95% of the global Hindu population. Nepal, with 24 million Hindus, Bangladesh with 13 million, Pakistan with 5 million and Indonesia with 4 million made up the other countries in the top five.The rankings are expected to change by 2070, with the United States projected to have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Australia is also expected to enter the top 10, ranking ninth with around 3 million Hindus, while the United Arab Emirates is projected to drop out of the list.Pakistan's Hindu population is expected to double to 10 million by 2070, although the country is projected to retain its fourth position in the global rankings.Outside India, much of the projected growth in the Hindu population is expected to come from Pakistan and the United States. Pakistan is likely to see an increase primarily through natural population growth, with births outnumbering deaths, while immigration is expected to be the main driver of growth in the US.Hindu population growth across regionsThe Asia-Pacific region, home to 99% of the world's Hindus, is projected to account for most of the community's growth over the next five decades. Its Hindu population is expected to increase by 191 million between 2020 and 2070.Hindus are projected to make up 28% of the region's population by 2070, compared with 26% in 2020.In North America, the Hindu population is expected to more than double from 4 million in 2020 to 9 million in 2070. Their share of the region's population is projected to increase from 1% to 2%.Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean are the only regions where the Hindu population is projected to decline in absolute numbers. If current trends continue, Hindus will account for less than 0.1% of the population in each of these regions by 2070.Fertility, migration and religious switching to shape Hindu populationPew's projections identify fertility, mortality, age structure, international migration and religious switching as the key factors determining changes in the size of religious groups.The global Hindu population is expected to gain more than 200 million people through natural increase between 2020 and 2070, with nearly all of this growth projected to take place in the Asia-Pacific region.Religious switching is expected to have little impact on the overall Hindu population. Pew said this is partly because Hindus have a high retention rate, with an estimated 99% of people raised Hindu continuing to identify with the religion as adults.The corresponding retention rates are 85% among Christians and 83% among Buddhists. Muslims have a retention rate of 99%, on a par with Hindus.Overall, religious switching is projected to reduce the global Hindu population by around 1 million people between 2020 and 2070, with most of the losses expected in the Asia-Pacific region.Migration, meanwhile, is expected to contribute significantly to Hindu population growth in North America, the Middle East-North Africa region and Europe. Together, these regions are projected to gain more than 8 million Hindus through migration by 2070.Asia and the Pacific is expected to record the largest migration-related losses. However, the region's gains through natural population growth are projected to far exceed the number of Hindus it loses through emigration.Islam projected to overtake Christianity as world's largest religionThe Pew report also projects that Islam will overtake Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, as the Muslim population continues to grow at a faster pace.Both religions are expanding globally, but Pew attributed the faster growth of Islam largely to higher fertility rates among Muslims.“It's the babies,” said Conrad Hackett, a senior demographer at Pew, explaining that fertility rates play a much greater role in religious population growth than conversion and other forms of religious switching.Also check:US will not have a Christian majority by 2027, religiously unaffiliated to make up 41%: Pew studyDuring 2020-2025, the fertility rate among Muslim women stood at 3.1 children per woman, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. The average for women belonging to all other religious groups was 1.6, below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman needed for each generation to replace itself.According to Pew's latest estimates, there were 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims worldwide in 2020. The new projections indicate that the Muslim population will reach 2.57 billion by 2035, overtaking the Christian population, which is expected to stand at 2.52 billion.If current trends continue, the number of Muslims worldwide will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population is projected to remain just below 3 billion.US projected to lose Christian majority by 2065The projections also point to significant changes in the religious composition of North America.The United States, where Christians currently account for 62% of the population, is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to make up 41% of the US population.In neighbouring Canada, Christians are projected to account for less than half of the population by 2030. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to outnumber Christians in the country.The rise in the number of people identifying with no religion is a significant factor behind the projected decline in the Christian share of the population in both countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl in France nearly 40 years ago
articles.summary: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.
articles.body:
The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.

The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.

Four-year-old Inass Touloub was found along the A10 road in Suèvres in the Loir-et-Cher department on 11 August 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.

She was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".

Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother – tested in an unrelated case – matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.

The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.

During the trial, prosecutor Anaïs Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.

The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.

French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.

El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.

Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.

articles.title: German chancellor warns Islamic immigrants, others to honor nation's Holocaust legacy or leave
articles.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz told Jewish athletes that immigrants from Islamic countries and elsewhere must honor Germany's Holocaust responsibility or leave the country.
articles.body: Eight decades after the Holocaust, Germany's conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that accepting the nation's responsibility for the Nazi genocide is an obligation that extends fully to immigrants arriving from Islamic countries. During an official reception for Germany’s Maccabiah Jewish sports delegation in Berlin on Nov. 6, Merz said the "historical responsibility of our country applies just as much to those who come here to Germany from Islamic countries, and anyone who fails to abide by this must leave our country." His response came after a basketball coach told him athletes feared being attacked if they wore their red Maccabi training jackets bearing the Star of David on German streets. The German Press Agency, dpa, reported that Merz quoted former German President Richard von Weizsäcker, who in 1985 told the Bundestag that "young people are not responsible" for the crimes of the Nazis, "but they are responsible for what becomes of it in history." Merz said the principle was "set in stone," and that, "given the current circumstances," von Weizsäcker’s words "also apply to immigrants who come to Germany," referring to recent antisemitic offenses committed by Muslim immigrants. GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS The chancellor’s office released his prepared remarks from the event, but did not include comments made in a question-and-answer session with the athletes. When asked by Fox News Digital about his statement, a German government spokesperson said, "The chancellor's words speak for themselves." "Chancellor Merz is not only right to make these remarks," said Sweden-based political scientist Daniel Schatz, "he is fulfilling Germany's historical responsibility." Schatz, who holds a doctorate from Berlin’s Humboldt University, says Merz’s statement reflects the German concept of "Staatsräson," or reason of state, "which places Germany's historical responsibility for the Holocaust and its commitment to Israel's security at the heart of German national and foreign policy." Schatz said Merz’s remarks point to a broader challenge for Germany. "When Jewish athletes in Germany and other parts of Europe are afraid to wear clothing displaying the Star of David, we are confronting something far more serious than a failure of integration," he said. "We are witnessing a failure of the state to guarantee that Jewish citizens can live openly and securely." "A country that has made 'Never Again' a cornerstone of its national identity cannot accept a situation in which Jewish identity must be concealed for reasons of personal safety." ITALY’S SCHOOL VEIL BAN EXPOSES EUROPE’S ASSIMILATION FIGHT AS EXPERT WARNS US COULD BE NEXT Simone Rodan‑Benzaquen, senior envoy to Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital, "Merz is right: everyone who makes Germany their home must accept the responsibility to protect Jewish life. You do not have to inherit Germany’s guilt to share that responsibility." "This is a fundamental question of integration," she added. "Learning German and finding a job matter, but integration also means accepting that your Jewish neighbor has the same right to live openly and safely as you do. That requires transparent foreign funding, scrutiny of what publicly supported organizations teach, enforcement against threats and violence, and support for Muslims challenging antisemitism within their own communities." SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER Since the Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack by Hamas, Janek Treiber, a Dresden University of Technology research fellow, said Germany "has seen a sort of culture war between those who argue for solidarity with Palestinians and view Israel as an oppressive state, and those who stand firmly with Israel. In Germany, this debate is naturally conducted with even greater intensity due to the country’s history." Despite the strength of Merz's remarks, Treiber said the comments have not generated the kind of reaction that has accompanied some of Merz’s previous comments on migration. "Most people would likely agree that anyone moving to Germany… must respect the constitutional order and come to terms with Germany’s historical legacy," Treiber said. "Merz’s words should not be a surprise to anyone," Rodan-Benzaquen said. "The measure of success will be whether those athletes can wear their team jackets on German streets without fear." articles.title: Pax Silica is the new face of US imperialism in the Philippines
articles.summary: Behind promises of jobs and investment lie threats to ancestral lands, water security and national sovereignty.
articles.body:
The Philippine government is promising jobs and billions in investment through the United States-led Pax Silica initiative. But protesters see a very different future: threatened ancestral lands, environmental destruction and deeper dependence on Washington.

On November 15, ahead of Donald Trump’s visit to Manila for the ASEAN summit, Philippine police arrested more than 200 demonstrators opposing the initiative. The arrests were part of a wider crackdown on protests against a project that critics see as another form of US neo-imperialism.

The Pax Silica initiative is a US-led coalition aimed at securing supply chains and countering China’s strength in critical minerals, semiconductors and other technologies essential to AI infrastructure. The Philippines joined the initiative in April 2026, with a proposed industrial hub in New Clark City, Tarlac province, forming part of it. The Philippine government has promoted the proposed industrial hub as essential to economic development, projecting that it could generate more than 130,000 jobs and attract up to $70bn in investment once fully developed, a process expected to take decades. The proposed Pax Silica industrial hub, which covers approximately 1,618 hectares, raises concerns not only about national sovereignty but also about the displacement of local communities, environmental repercussions, Indigenous land rights and human security.

Critics see the project as taking land from local communities and farmers to serve foreign interests. The Aeta Hungey community in Sapang Kawayan, for example, faces relocation from land it has occupied for generations. Around 200 residents could lose access to their homes, farmland, water sources and burial grounds, while the community’s efforts to secure formal recognition of its ancestral land, dating back to 1994, remain unresolved.

Another major concern is water consumption. According to the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), the proposed industrial hub could require 65–90 million litres of water daily. Although the BCDA plans to meet this demand through surface-water harvesting, concerns remain about the pressure on water resources, particularly during droughts. The Philippines is already vulnerable to drought, water shortages, agricultural disruption and climate change. On November 4, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) confirmed that a very strong El Nino was present and expected to persist into the first half of 2027.

The Philippine government must respond to the pressing needs of Filipinos instead of becoming a pawn of the United States in its geopolitical rivalry with China. Southeast Asia is a focal point of competition between the two major powers, with the Philippines serving as a key US ally. Pax Silica would position the Philippines as a central node in an emerging AI Cold War with China.

Projected as an avenue for economic progress, Pax Silica could also serve as a tool for the military expansion of the US in the region, particularly in the Philippines. Semiconductors are used in modern military production and are essential components of weapon systems in modern warfare. During his November 17 ASEAN speech, Trump highlighted US agreements across the region involving critical minerals, energy and technology, while describing the Philippines as a longstanding key ally. He also pointed to increased defence cooperation between the two countries. This cooperation already rests in part on the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), which allows US forces access to agreed Philippine military facilities.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr also emphasised the depth of the relationship between the two countries, rooted in shared history and values. Describing the extent of US influence in Philippine life, he said, “There is no part of our lives in the Philippines that is not involved with the United States in some way, in some shape or form or another.”

An unexamined alliance compromises national interests, particularly those affecting the lives of the Filipino people. Economic development should not come at the expense of human security, sovereignty and environmental sustainability.

Against this backdrop, a broad, multisectoral opposition movement against Pax Silica has emerged and is gaining momentum. It brings together diverse sectors, including Indigenous peoples, farmers, workers, scientists, environmentalists, faith leaders, students, and progressive activists.

The protests have also spread to university campuses. On November 13, university students staged coordinated campus walkouts across the Philippines. Among the major participating universities were the University of the Philippines, De La Salle University, Ateneo de Manila University, University of Santo Tomas, and Far Eastern University, among others. United in their opposition to Pax Silica, protesters repeatedly chanted slogans denouncing US imperialism. Drawing on the Philippines’ history as a former US colony, they associate the initiative with another neocolonial project by an imperial power.

In the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Mindanao, where anti-Pax Silica demonstrations took place in Marawi City and Tawi-Tawi, the opposition is particularly significant. For protesters in this predominantly Muslim region, opposition to the initiative intersects with longstanding grievances rooted in the historical dispossession of local communities whose ancestral lands were taken by settlers, reinforced by imperialist wars and oppression. They see Pax Silica as another project that could displace local communities and facilitate land-grabbing by an imperial power.

Equally important is the movement’s expansion beyond the Philippines into transnational solidarity. According to organisers, solidarity demonstrations have taken place in 23 cities across 14 countries, bringing international support to the opposition against Pax Silica and US imperialism.

As the movement gains momentum, the Marcos administration must address the legitimate grievances of the people directly affected by the proposed project. Moreover, this is not merely a concern of the Indigenous Aeta communities; it carries broader regional implications. Marcos’s reference to shared history does not necessarily mean that the two countries stand on equal footing. There is no symmetrical relationship between a coloniser and a colonised. Those subjected to imperial domination are not equal to those imposing control.

The ASEAN Way, characterised by the principle of consensus, must prevail over the competing interests of major powers. Fostering multilateralism will pave the way for cooperation, collective security and economic progress that will eventually empower ASEAN and the Global South. It is through this approach that the three major priorities of the Philippine ASEAN chairship can be realised: Peace and Security Anchors, Prosperity Corridors, and People Empowerment.

articles.title: Surrey group completes Heathrow to Rome Fiat 500 challenge
articles.summary: Stuart Bailey and a group of men took £500 Fiats from Heathrow to Rome in three days, raising £13,000.
articles.body:
The organisers of a challenge that saw a group of men drive £500 Fiat 500s from Heathrow to Rome said they felt an "overwhelming sense of pride" on returning home having raised £13,000 for charity.

Stuart Bailey, from Rusper, West Sussex, organised the 4,000km (2,485 mile) trip for the Movember men's health charity, taking 27 people from Heathrow to the Italian capital in three days.

The group, due to arrive in Newdigate, Surrey, on Wednesday, took five months to prepare for the challenge, with all eight cars making the trip in one piece.

Bailey said: "The cause is so important. Movember is genuinely making a difference to men's health, and we're still fundraising to reach our £20,000 target."

He added: "There's an incredible and overwhelming sense of pride and achievement in watching the team arrive back today."

The group, who also employed a team of four mechanics to keep the cars running, said the Fiats faced a number of issues, including problems with the gearbox and suspension.

The cars were given themed names, including Mo-ana, Hercule Poi-mo, Scarlett Mo'Hara and the Mo-na Lisa, and the teams completed the first leg in fancy dress.

On arriving in Rome, some of the men involved swapped places with their wives and partners, who drove the cars back to the UK on the return leg.

Following the event, the cars are due to be auctioned off to raise more funds.

articles.summary: David Smith says he wants Susan Smith to stay in prison until she dies for killing their sons as the South Carolina parole board weighs her request.
articles.body: Susan Smith’s ex-husband wants her to remain in prison until she dies for killing their two sons in what prosecutors say was a bid to win back her lover, as a seven-member board prepares to consider her parole request Thursday. David Smith, 56, made the comments to CNN as the South Carolina Board of Paroles and Pardons prepares to hear his ex-wife's request for parole in the 1994 murders of her children, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander. "If I have a choice, I’d want her to stay in prison until she dies," David Smith said. "32 years hasn’t changed the heartache." While Susan Smith was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to life in prison in 1995, state law at the time allowed her to be considered for parole after serving 30 years. That law was changed shortly after her conviction, making people sentenced to life for a murder committed after Jan. 1, 1996 ineligible for parole. articles.title: UP police constable, girlfriend hire shooters to kill husband after she tells lover he talks to other women
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A serving Uttar Pradesh Police constable allegedly conspired with his girlfriend to get her husband murdered and hired contract killers for Rs 6
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A serving Uttar Pradesh Police constable allegedly conspired with his girlfriend to get her husband murdered and hired contract killers for Rs 6 lakh, police said on Wednesday. The conspiracy came to light after the woman’s husband, Anurag Shukla, was shot at near Purnia crossing in Aliganj on October 28. He survived the attack but sustained a bullet injury to his right arm."The Aliganj police, along with the north zone SWAT and surveillance teams, arrested five people, including the woman, Aashi Mishra, and constable Nitin Rana, in connection with the case. Four of the accused were arrested near Maliyana crossing in Meerut, while Aashi was arrested in Lucknow," said DCP North Amit K Anand.According to the DCP, Rana, who is currently posted at the Lucknow Reserve Police Lines, had been in a relationship with Aashi since 2022. "The two allegedly met while preparing for competitive examinations at a public library in Lucknow. Aashi married Anurag in 2025 but allegedly remained in contact with Rana," the officer added.Police said the two hatched a plan to eliminate Anurag after Aashi allegedly told Rana that her husband was talking to other women. They fixed a contract of Rs 6 lakh to have him killed. Rana subsequently contacted his acquaintances, including Mayank Vashisht alias Lala and Shubham Sharma, to execute the plan.As part of the conspiracy, the accused allegedly visited Lucknow on October 26 and conducted reconnaissance of Anurag’s movements and routine. Two days later, around 10.30 pm, Mayank and Manoj Rajput allegedly opened fire on him near the Matulya fast food outlet, close to the Central Building gate at Purnia crossing. Anurag sustained a bullet injury to his right arm.The accused fled after the attack. Police said Rana later called the other accused to Meerut to plan another attempt on Anurag’s life. Acting on CCTV footage, mobile surveillance and other technical evidence, the joint police team tracked them down and arrested four accused in Meerut. Aashi was subsequently arrested in Lucknow.Those arrested have been identified as Mayank Vashisht, Shubham Sharma, Shivam Rajput, Nitin Rana and Aashi Mishra. Manoj Rajput, who allegedly fired at Anurag along with Mayank, is absconding, and efforts are underway to arrest him, police said.Police said the accused told investigators that the firearm used in the attack had been discarded somewhere along the way. Four mobile phones and Rs 1,360 in cash were recovered from them. articles.summary: U.S. embassies in London, Berlin and Madrid issued holiday security alerts to traveling Americans, urging people to stay vigilant at festivals, markets and transit hubs.

"U.S. citizens should exercise extra vigilance at holiday festivals and events and other locations with large crowds," it also says. Officials added that visitors to congested and popular tourist areas should pay particular attention to their surroundings and always follow the instructions of police and emergency response officials. articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12 just launched this past fall, and it’s already $70 off
articles.summary: The Apple Watch Series 12, the brand’s newest smartwatch, is already on sale. It’s a great upgrade for anyone who wants detailed health tracking and faster charging.
articles.body: In the spirit of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the Apple Watch Series 12 is up to $70 off on Amazon, bringing the 42mm GPS model down to its lowest price ever. That’s a pretty rare drop for a smartwatch that just came out in September, and it’s the Series 12’s first major discount since launch. The Apple Watch has consistently been one of the best fitness trackers we’ve tested here at NBC Selected, with the previous Series 11 being the best smartwatch for anyone with an iPhone. So if you’ve been waiting to upgrade an older Apple Watch, or you want a holiday gift for someone that tracks their health around the clock, keep reading to find out more about this deal and why you won’t want to wait to grab it. The Series 12 is Apple’s newest flagship smartwatch, and its biggest upgrade is a redesigned Health Sensing System powered by the new S11 chip. It checks your heart rate in the background every five seconds and measures heart rate variability far more often than the Series 11, according to Apple. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans — who’s currently testing the Series 12 — bought the previous watch for her sister to monitor her heart rate and other health stats. “It’s easy to set up and sync. I just love that it gives me peace of mind that if something is off with her heart health, she has a tool that can send her an alert and do an ECG,” she says. But if you ever feel too inundated with tons of biometric data, I like that the watch combines your activity and sleep into an easy-to-read “readiness score” each morning, so you have some foundational information about how hard to push yourself that day. Unlike Oura and Whoop, Apple doesn’t charge a subscription for Readiness or its other health features. Battery life still tops out at 24 hours of normal use, but thankfully charging has gotten much faster: 15 minutes on the charger adds up to 12 hours of use, 50% more than the Series 11. If you’re hitting the trail or completing an outdoor workout, that uses up to 10 hours of battery. You also get new Siri features, including Live Rewind, which replays the last 15 seconds of any audio you missed. (Note: This is a feature you have to enable, it’s not automatic.) While the discount may not seem like a lot compared to deals we typically feature (for comparison, the Apple Watch SE 3 is currently 20% off), it’s a surprising sale considering the smartwatch just launched this fall. The price might drop further when Black Friday officially arrives, it might not (or it could sell out before that). If it’s been on your radar as a purchase for the holidays, now’s the time to grab it. The 46mm model has the same features in a larger case with a bigger display, which makes texts and workout stats easier to read at a glance. It’s down to $379 from $429, also its lowest price ever. As someone who owns a Series 11, I’d still say the upgrade is modest. The Series 12 makes the most sense if you’re coming from a Series 9 or older, or looking to gift someone their very first Apple Watch. articles.title: Charlotte wants Iryna Zarutska murder lawsuit tossed, says it can’t be held responsible
articles.summary: Charlotte argues governmental immunity shields its transit policing decisions as it asks a judge to toss Iryna Zarutska's family's wrongful-death lawsuit.
articles.body: The city of Charlotte is asking a judge to throw out a wrongful-death lawsuit filed by Iryna Zarutska's family over security failures they say left her unprotected aboard the city's light-rail system, arguing many of those decisions are protected by governmental immunity. Zarutska's murder drew national attention after surveillance video showed Decarlos Brown Jr. seated behind her aboard a Lynx Blue Line train before he is accused of stabbing her in the neck about four minutes after she boarded. The 23-year-old Ukrainian refugee had just left work at a local pizzeria. Her family alleges Charlotte failed to adequately police and secure the light-rail system. The city now argues decisions involving transit policing, crime prevention, security contractors and public safety are government functions shielded from liability under North Carolina law. PROSECUTORS SAY CHARLOTTE TRAIN STABBING CASE WON'T BE DISMISSED REGARDLESS OF COMPETENCY RULING Charlotte's new filing also acknowledges there was no private security guard inside Zarutska's train car when she was killed, that Brown apparently boarded without presenting a ticket or pass and that the light-rail system operates without turnstiles or fare gates. But the city denies those circumstances caused Zarutska's death, arguing Brown acted on his own and that the attack could not have been predicted based on previous crime across the transit system. DEATH OF GREAT-GRANDMOTHER BRUTALLY KILLED ON TRAIN TRIGGERS FEDERAL ACTION Zarutska's family sued Charlotte and its private transit security contractor, Professional Police Services, or PSS, in August, alleging security failures left riders vulnerable to violent crime. Charlotte responded Monday with a 34-page filing asking a Mecklenburg County Superior Court judge to throw out the claims against the city. MURAL HONORING MURDERED UKRAINIAN REFUGEE IRYNA ZARUTSKA TAKEN DOWN IN PROVIDENCE AFTER LOCAL OUTRAGE The city says the lawsuit challenges "law-enforcement deployment, transit policing, crime prevention, security-contractor oversight, and public-safety administration" and argues those activities are protected by governmental immunity. Zarutska's family anticipated that defense in its lawsuit, arguing Charlotte waived immunity and that operating a light-rail system that charges fares amounts to a proprietary rather than governmental function. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The family's complaint alleges stronger fare enforcement, physical barriers and adequate security could have prevented Brown from boarding the train or carrying out the attack. It cites findings from the North Carolina state auditor showing Charlotte and the Charlotte Area Transit System (CATS) planned to spend about $2.23 million on safety and security equipment in 2025 but spent about $470,000, leaving roughly $1.76 million unspent and some planned security work unfinished.
